newsitem.title: USA: Burlington Northern closes N. Dakota lines.
newsitem.headline: Burlington Northern closes N. Dakota lines.

text.p: Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railway said heavy snow and high winds overnight closed its main lines in North Dakota overnight.
Floodwaters from Lake Pepin near Minneapolis-St Paul, Minnesota, also closed its main line between Chicago and Minneapolis, a company spokesman said.
"We cannot ship cargo from Chicago to the Twin Cities at this moment," Burlington Northern spokesman Jim Sabourin said in a telephone interview.

He said the main line between Chicago and the Twin Cities was closed Sunday night just south of St Paul due to wave action on Lake Pepin. "We had some heavy waves on the lake that would be affecting our track," he said.

He said the track was expected to reopen Monday afternoon. "However, the upper Mississippi River continues to rise in the Twin Cities area and we fully expect our lines to be closed again by floodwaters on Wednesday," he said.
He said a three-mile section of railroad track was out of service near Savage, Minnesota.
According to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the Minnesota River at Savage was 10 feet above flood stage late Sunday. It is due to crest at 16 feet above flood level on April 14, the Corps said.

Also in North Dakota, heavy snow and high winds over the weekend closed Burlington's main lines between Glendive, Montana, and Dilworth, Minnesota, between Fargo and Grand Forks, North Dakota, between Grand Forks and Minot, North Dakota, and in the vicinity of Hettinger, North Dakota, Burlington Northern said.
"Those are our major northern lines" that were closed over the weekend, Sabourin said.

"We expect to them to be reopen late today (Monday) or early Tuesday," Sabourin said. "As of now they are closed. All of our shipments are experiencing a minimum of 24 hours delay as we work to reroute."
